rulings.reason: JSON sent between systems is UTF-8 by definition (RFC 8259). json-output.md:42 and :47 settle the framing: each payload is one compact line, and the stream is newline-delimited JSON. The job needed no separate encoding statement.
json-output.md:42 says every payload is one compact line, and :47 calls the stream newline-delimited JSON. A line-based reader needs nothing more, and the code matches (doctor.go:105 writes "%s\n").
The line framing is stated at json-output.md:42 and :47, and UTF-8 is inherent to JSON interchange. No missing fact blocked the parser.

json-output.md:25-26 says every payload except a per-site NDJSON line carries exitCode, and :149 says the same. The health schema description (line 5) says only the stream form omits it, so the single-site case is settled.

json-output.md:25-26 and :149, plus the health schema description at line 5, state that single-site `cairn health <site>` carries exitCode and only stream lines omit it. The caller also knows which command form it ran.

cairn-adopt-list.schema.json:8 and :20 declare additionalProperties:false, and json-output.md:38 makes the schema normative. Yet json-output.md:346-348 says a field was added within schemaVersion 1 and older readers still read every candidate. No published page says whether readers must tolerate unknown properties.

The reader departed from the page because two statements conflict: the closed schema (adopt-list schema line 8, additionalProperties:false) and json-output.md:346-348, which promises older readers survive fields added within v1. No page gives a rule on unknown fields.
A parser needs to know whether to tolerate unknown fields. json-output.md:346-348 implies tolerance while every schema sets additionalProperties:false, and no published page states the rule.

doctor.md:117-119 and :123-124 limit exit 3 to three cases. json-output.md:432-440 and :485-489 show a doctor payload with a warning-severity fail plus an unknown at exitCode 3, which follows from the precedence at exit-codes.md:26. A tool fault also exits 3 with no payload (doctor.go:55-57).

doctor.md:123 says any other exit 3 is a run whose only non-passing results are UNCHECKED. The doctor example (json-output.md:413-414, :432-439, :485-489) has a warning FAIL (doctor.md:81) plus an UNCHECKED at exit 3, because UNKNOWN outranks WARNING (exit-codes.md:26).

doctor.md:121-122 says a usage error is the one no-payload case. But doctor.go:55-57 returns an error before any payload when doctor.NewSnapshot fails, and exit-codes.md:95-97 lists a run that ended early and a tool fault as further empty-stdout cases.

No contradiction here. The doctor schema's state enum (line 28) is the shared frozen five-word set, while json-output.md:399-403 says doctor writes only those frozen words and never writes held. A permissive enum does not conflict with a value that is never emitted.

exit-codes.md:83-84 says a missing-credential auth row carries `reason.cred-missing`, but json-output.md:376-377 says an authCheck row's reason is display text, not a vocabulary code. The code matches json-output: probe_token.go:170 uses authCheckCredMissingReason, which produces the text "%s is not set" (messages.go:545-549).

json-output.md:320 is about the logs personal-data notice, which --json keeps off stderr. That fits line 13's rule that stderr carries diagnostics, and logs.go:71-77 confirms stderr carries nothing but an error under --json. The two lines do not contradict.

doctor.md:10 refers to the seven checks that need a deployed site, which doctor.md:128-129 lists. That does not claim `cairn health` has only seven checks, so it does not contradict the nine ids at json-output.md:501-502.

json-output.md:17-19 says the payload's exitCode is the process exit code and never disagrees with the verdict, and exit-codes.md:7-8 says an --expect-sites mismatch exits 3. A wrapper reading exitCode has what it needs, and the code folds the mismatch into errors (sites.go:80-81), which matches json-output.md:301-302.
